summary: Derived the universal founding bridge from four typed premises over an agency vocabulary (attestation by the resurrection, divine veracity applied to confirmation, the mandate's scope over Jesus' founding with a teaching commission, envoy founding, restricted to Jesus as envoy). The society-universal is carried by the scope premise, not derived. Omission models show each premise necessary; a joint model shows the premises and every stage antecedent satisfiable. Newly pinned Acts 17 and John 13; the attestation premise is read from Acts 17.31, Matthew 28.18-20, John 13.20 and Dei Filius ch. 3 para. 1 support the other three. All four premises remain open; the scope premise's universal reach over societies and the eleven-to-society map are unsourced. The bare bridge leaves the frontier; route costs rise by 3. Not established: the bridge's truth, any premise, or historical fidelity. Definition audit (2026-11-06): explicit direct-only and Jesus-envoy-inclusive calibration propositions now separate a stipulated word sense from the primitive target predicate. Named-only coverage is open; excluded middle gives I or E or neither, without eliminating either named reading. Five schema interpretations witness overlap, each named reading alone, and neither with the old envoy bridge true or false. Minimal direct calibration does not itself refute the bridge: on that reading the bridge holds exactly when each commissioned Jesus-envoy founding is also direct. The stronger Jesus-scope exclusion plus a nonempty commissioned event does refute it; no Jesus/God distinctness or all-creature exclusion was derived. The event follows from the existing stage antecedents plus attestation, veracity and universal mandate scope. The bridge formula itself never required HoldsMandate. No source claim or frozen Challenge changed. The new conditional routes add three bare framework inputs and do not discharge a root premise.
